messages.content:
You are a C test designer. Design high-level test scenarios (WHAT to test), not C code (HOW).

ROLE: Phase 1 of dual-phase architecture
- You: Design test for ONE execution path
- Phase 2: Converts your design to C code

INPUTS PROVIDED:
- Function signature, description, implementation (source code)
- ONE target execution path with conditions
- Operation map (available helper functions)

YOUR TASKS:
1. Analyze path: What conditions trigger it? What inputs? Expected behavior?
2. Study implementation: Understand branches, variables, edge cases for this path
3. Design test: Choose inputs that trigger path conditions (boundary, normal, edge, error cases)
4. Specify helpers: Assertions, utilities, dependencies from operation map
5. Define expectations: Return values, side effects, state changes, invariants
6. Provide rationale: Why this test matters, what bugs it catches

NO MOCKING ALLOWED:
Do NOT design tests requiring: mock functions, forced failures, simulated allocation failures, faked system calls.
ONLY use: Real inputs, natural error conditions (NULL, invalid params), actual boundary values.

Example - WRONG: "Test malloc failure handling" (requires mock_malloc_fail)
Example - RIGHT: "Test NULL pointer handling" (pass NULL directly)

SUCCESS CRITERIA:
✓ Test exercises the target path with correct inputs
✓ All assertions, helpers, dependencies specified
✓ Rationale clear and convincing
✓ Memory management specified (setup/cleanup)
✓ Valid JSON output with all required fields
✓ Test naming: test_<function>_<path_scenario>

OUTPUT: JSON object with metadata, test_scenarios array (1 scenario for the path), test_suite_summary.

test_metadata.description: Verify quickSort does not recurse or modify the array when sorting a single-element subarray (low == high).
test_metadata.rationale: This test ensures the function correctly handles the minimal boundary case, avoiding unnecessary recursion or modification, and prevents off-by-one or infinite recursion bugs.

expected_branches: if (low < high) → false → skip body → implicit return

primary.name: quickSort
primary.signature: void quickSort(int arr[], int low, int high)

dependencies.name: partition
dependencies.signature: int partition(int arr[], int low, int high)
dependencies.reason: Would be called if (low < high) is true, but must NOT be called for this path
dependencies.call_path: quickSort → partition (not taken in this path)

dependencies.name: swap
dependencies.reason: Used by partition, but not reached in this path
dependencies.call_path: quickSort → partition → swap (not taken in this path)

assertions.name: assert_array_equal
assertions.purpose: Verify the array remains unchanged after quickSort
assertions.usage: Compare the array before and after sorting

utilities.name: create_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Allocate and initialize an integer array for testing

utilities.name: helper_copy_int_array
utilities.purpose: Create a deep copy of the array for later comparison
utilities.usage: Setup: preserve original array for post-sort comparison

utilities.name: cleanup_int_test_array
utilities.purpose: Deallocate the test array after the test

preconditions: Array is non-NULL and contains exactly one element
setup_requirements.initial_state: A single-element array is allocated and initialized (e.g., [42])

primary_function_args.test_value_semantic: Pointer to a single-element integer array
primary_function_args.rationale: Triggers the (low >= high) path; minimal non-empty array
Start index of the single-element subarray
End index equals start index for single-element

return_value.description: No return value; function completes without error

assertions_required.description: Verify the array is unchanged after quickSort
assertions_required.failure_meaning: Function modified the array when it should not have

cleanup_requirements.final_state: All allocated arrays are freed; no memory leaks

edge_cases_to_note: Do not use NULL array (not allowed by contract)
Do not use low > high (would be a different path, but still valid to test elsewhere)

path_coverage_analysis.description: Base case: (low >= high) so quickSort returns immediately, no recursion or partition.

integration_test_suggestions: Test quickSort on multi-element arrays to cover recursive and partitioning paths.
Test quickSort with low > high to confirm immediate return (no-op).
